root_cause_investigation.finding: 100% failure rate in September (40/40 runs) is driven entirely by the REQUIRED 'enforce-venv-python' job (the soft-launched, continue-on-error Windows job is unrelated to overall run conclusion). Sampled run 34629171322 (2026-09-11): the 'Run governance test suite' step fails with '1 failed, 1594 passed, 44 skipped' -- a SINGLE deterministic test assertion failure (kind: value_mismatch), not flakiness: registry.PLATFORM_CONTRACT declares 6 platforms (python, go, net, java, rust, cpp) for the example_verification site, but platform_capabilities.yaml has no corresponding row for any of them.
root_cause_investigation.classification: PRODUCT_DEFECT (a real content-pipeline configuration gap: platform_capabilities.yaml is missing rows the registry contract declares) -- NOT a CI workflow defect, NOT flaky, NOT a dependency outage.
root_cause_investigation.cost_impact: This single unfixed config gap is directly responsible for a 100% failure rate on the #3 cost driver (326 min/21.8% of total this period) -- every one of those minutes was spent on a run that was always going to fail.
root_cause_investigation.scope_note: Fixing platform_capabilities.yaml is outside MT069's mandate (GH Actions cost/infra, not content-pipeline configuration) -- flagging for separate attention, not fixing here. Self-hosting (MT069-PHB-07) does not fix or worsen this -- the same test will fail at the same rate regardless of where the job runs.

root_cause_investigation.finding: 49% failure rate in September (98/200 runs) is NOT a single recurring bug -- sampled 3 different failed runs and found 3 DIFFERENT blocking causes: run 34681458190 blocked on 'check_evaluator_version_bump.py' (scripts/pipeline/content_eval/evaluators/description_completeness.py changed without a version bump); run 34630174372 blocked on the same check but a different evaluator (capability_claim_check.py); run 34638073599 failed for a different reason not yet isolated. DIFF_BASE (the parent-commit comparison point) correctly varies per run -- ruled out a stuck/broken diff-base as the cause.
root_cause_investigation.classification: PROCESS_DISCIPLINE_GAP, not a CI/workflow defect -- the check is correctly catching real evaluator-version-bump policy violations at a high, recurring rate, suggesting whoever/whatever edits scripts/pipeline/content_eval/evaluators/*.py (likely multiple concurrent agent sessions, per this repo's own documented concurrency hazards) frequently forgets to bump EVALUATOR_VERSIONS.
root_cause_investigation.cost_impact: A failed push here likely gets fixed and re-pushed (bump added), meaning each real logical change can cost 2x the CI minutes (one failing run, one passing re-run) on the #1 cost driver (546 min/36.5% of total).
root_cause_investigation.scope_note: Also outside MT069's mandate to fix (a content-pipeline authoring-discipline issue, not a GH Actions infra issue). Same self-hosting note as above: hosting location doesn't change this failure rate.

root_cause_investigation.finding: 100% failure rate, all recorded history (58/58 historical, 14/14 in September) -- this workflow has never once succeeded.
root_cause_investigation.classification: CORRECTED TWICE, same day (2026-09-18). Pass 1 disproved 'missing pip install' (zero third-party imports, runs fine locally) and wrongly concluded this was a healthy gate correctly reporting real gaps. Pass 2, after actually dispatching the migrated schedule leg on a real fresh checkout, found the true root cause: launch_dashboard.py's real inputs (reports/phase_state.json, reports/human-review/**, reports/**/readiness.md) are gitignored, cumulative local state (project_phase_store.py) never available in ANY fresh checkout. Real dispatched result: NO REPORT: 33/33, Gaps: 99 -- not the 2-gap result the local-only test showed. CONFIRMED_DEFECT stands, but for a structural data-availability reason, not a missing pip-install crash and not 'healthy, no defect' either.
root_cause_investigation.cost_impact: Low (17 min/1.1% of total) -- 100% of this cost currently produces a report with zero real content.
root_cause_investigation.scope_note: ORIGINAL (superseded): candidate for a quick, safe fix (add the missing pip install step) IF launch_dashboard.py has third-party dependencies -- still needs that source verification per HP-11's original deferral reasoning, not done in this pass. RESOLUTION (2026-09-18, two passes): no dependencies exist, so no pip-install fix was ever relevant; the real fix is a script-level redesign (stop depending on gitignored local state) or retiring this as a CI job entirely -- neither attempted here, see dossiers/launch-dashboard.md for full detail and the two-pass correction history.

root_cause_investigation.finding: 93.3% historical failure rate (14/15), 1/1 in the September sample.
root_cause_investigation.classification: CORRECTED 2026-09-18: originally classified CONFIRMED_DEFECT per TC-03's HP-05 as a 'PAT gap, issue #94' -- this was a misdiagnosis. Direct source read of repo_patrol.py's cmd_sweep() plus a live repro found the real cause: clone_exists() is a pure filesystem check against the gitignored runs/.clone_cache/, never present on a fresh checkout, with zero token involvement. Fixed in Aspose/aspose.org commit 72821fbb4a (ensure_clone() auto-clone self-heal), tested (78/78 passing), verified live end-to-end.
root_cause_investigation.cost_impact: Negligible (2 min/0.1% of total) -- the significance here is correctness/reliability of upstream-drift monitoring, not cost.
root_cause_investigation.scope_note: RESOLVED 2026-09-18 -- fixed at the source, not deferred. No human PAT-provisioning decision was ever needed; issue #94 should be closed as a misdiagnosis.

workflows_with_zero_recorded_runs_in_the: Install Defect Sweep (durability) / install-literal-sweep.yml -- zero runs found in 1767 retrieved records across 172 days. RESOLVED (TC-11 independent review, 2026-09-17; re-verified independently via `git log --follow --diff-filter=A`): NOT 'despite being a weekly-scheduled bot [present the whole time]' -- the workflow was added 2026-09-10 (commit f9cbe210fb), so it was only ever eligible to fire once (Monday 2026-09-14, weekly 11:00 UTC schedule) inside the 172-day window before the mass-disable. Zero recorded runs is fully explained by young file age plus mass-disable timing -- not a broken trigger or a data-pull gap.
